title: The Sigil of Ironhollow
premise: Wren Brightwater was exiled at sixteen to Ironhollow, a mist-locked valley where magic cannot follow, and has built a quiet life there — until a stranger named Corren arrives on a date that matches a prophecy written a century before the kingdom that made it ceased to exist. The prophecy names Wren as the storm-caller who must reopen the Sigil of Ironhollow, the ancient door sealing the valley from a world now ruled by the Ashen Court, which is hunting the last dragon whose dying fire keeps the door's key alive. Pursued by the Court's hollow-eyed wardens and betrayed by the valley elder who arranged his exile, Wren must choose between the belonging he finally found and the justice owed to everyone the Court erased. In the end he reopens the Sigil not by force but by returning his stolen memories of home, letting the last dragon die free — and walks out of Ironhollow carrying the valley's name into a world that must learn it existed.
about_author: Kestrel Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the marginalia of forgotten regional fantasy presses. They write about exile, small communities, and the stubborn persistence of places the powerful would prefer forgotten.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the eve of his first date in nine years, Wren tends the lighthouse-lamps of Ironhollow and reflects on how the valley erases memory of the outside world. He finds an old book in the lamp-room archive: a prophecy dated a century past, naming tonight. Emotional beat: restless hope shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Tide Gate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. His date, Corren, arrives — and Wren recognizes him from the prophecy's illustration, down to the scar on his jaw. Corren claims he walked through a door that shouldn't exist, fleeing riders with hollow eyes. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as the first warden's lantern appears on the ridge.

chapters.title: What the Mist Keeps Out
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Corren explains the world beyond: the Ashen Court burned the kingdom of Vel Saren off every map and record, and Ironhollow is the last place its name survives. The wardens want the valley's archive. Emotional beat: guilt, as Corren realizes he led them straight to the last unburned library.

chapters.title: The Elder's Kindness
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Elder Maren Voss convenes the valley council and offers shelter to Corren — too readily, Wren thinks. Maren privately warns Wren that the prophecy also names 'the exile who remembers,' and only one person in Ironhollow was ever exiled within it: Wren himself. Emotional beat: unease beneath maternal warmth.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Wardens breach the outer mist using a captured dragon-scale compass. The valley's edge burns cold and colorless where they touch it. Corren and Wren evacuate the archive, saving one crate: the Sigil records. Emotional beat: first shared danger forging reluctant trust.

chapters.title: The Prophecy Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. By lamplight, Wren reads the full prophecy: a storm-caller will open the Sigil when the last dragon-fire gutters out, and the door will lead to a country that no longer exists. Wren confesses he can no longer remember why he was exiled — the valley took those memories as payment for sanctuary. Emotional beat: grief for a self he can't retrieve.

chapters.title: Hollow Eyes
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. A warden corners them; Corren recognizes her as his sister, Sef, taken by the Court years ago, her eyes emptied of everything but duty. She lets them go — for one hour — before the compulsion reclaims her. Emotional beat: heartbreak establishing what the Court does to people it erases.

chapters.title: The Dragon Beneath the Lake
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the Sigil records, they find the valley's heart: a drowned temple where the last dragon, Emberlain, sleeps coiled around the door-key — her own heart-flame. She is dying, and her fire is the only thing keeping the Sigil sealed against the Court. Emotional beat: awe and terrible responsibility.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Maren reveals she engineered Wren's exile-within-exile: she took his memories because the prophecy required a storm-caller who had forgotten his crime. She believes opening the Sigil dooms the valley. Emotional beat: betrayal — the closest thing Wren has to a mother confesses she unmade him.

chapters.title: The Crime Without a Name
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Digging through the saved crate, Corren finds Wren's confiscated trial record: at sixteen, Wren called a storm that killed three people — defending a friend from valley vigilantes, unjustly accused. The valley punished the victim. Emotional beat: righteous fury on Wren's behalf, and Wren's numb disbelief.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts the council with the truth of his trial. Some elders knew; some profited. The valley fractures — those who want to open the Sigil and face the world honestly, and those who would seal it forever over Emberlain's corpse. Emotional beat: Wren choosing principle over comfort for the first time.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Emberlain's fire dims sharply; the mist thins and wardens pour through the gaps. The valley's lamps fail one by one. Corren carries wounded children through falling ash while Sef, half-herself again, fights beside him without knowing why. Emotional beat: desperate courage amid collapse.

chapters.title: Sef Remembers Rain
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Sheltering in the lamp-room, Corren sings a childhood song and something flickers back in Sef — a memory of rain in a country that no longer exists. She begs him to finish what the prophecy started before the Court takes her fully. Emotional beat: fragile hope inside inevitable loss.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the drowned temple, the Sigil reveals its terms: it opens for one who returns what the valley took — Wren must surrender his remaining memories of Ironhollow itself, including Corren, Maren, everyone. Opening the door means walking through it having forgotten why he fought. Emotional beat: devastating choice between self and purpose.

chapters.title: Storm-Caller
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wardens storm the temple; Maren, repentant, holds the line with the council loyalists and dies buying Wren time. Her last words: 'Remembering isn't the same as keeping.' Wren raises his first true storm in nine years. Emotional beat: catharsis through grief-fueled power.

chapters.title: The Handing Over
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Corren reaches Wren at the altar and offers an alternative found in the records: the memories needn't be destroyed, only carried out — given to someone leaving anyway. He volunteers to carry Wren's memories of Ironhollow into the world. Emotional beat: love expressed as willingness to be forgotten.

chapters.title: Emberlain's Last Fire
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The dragon wakes enough to speak: she has guarded the door out of duty to a dead kingdom and asks, at last, to be released. Wren uses her final flame to ignite the Sigil rather than hoard it, freeing her to die under open sky. Emotional beat: mercy as the story's moral center.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vel Saren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Sigil opens onto the ghost-country: a preserved echo of Vel Saren on the night of its burning, where the erased dead wait to be remembered. Wren speaks their names aloud, learned from the archive, and the echo dissolves into ordinary morning light. Emotional beat: mourning transfigured into witness.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court Falls Quiet
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. With the country remembered, the Court's power — built on collective forgetting — collapses; wardens wake weeping, Sef among them, whole. The Ashen Regent turns to ash mid-decree. Emotional beat: justice arriving not as vengeance but as restoration.

chapters.title: What Corren Carries
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Outside the closing door, Corren holds Wren's memories of Ironhollow — every lamp lit, every festival, every moment of them together — and must decide whether to return them or keep them safe forever. He chooses to give them back. Emotional beat: tenderness at the cost of losing what he loves.

chapters.title: The Storm Returns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Memories restored, Wren stands in the real world for the first time in nine years, the valley behind him now open to the sky. He calls a gentle rain over the refugees streaming out of Ironhollow — the first weather the valley has ever known. Emotional beat: arrival, at last, into belonging.

chapters.title: The Name We Carry Out
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, epilogue. One year later, Wren and Corren teach in a rebuilt border town; a stone from the Sigil marks the valley road, and travelers speak of Ironhollow without fear. Wren lights a lamp each night for Maren, Emberlain, and Sef, who stayed to rebuild. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — memory kept alive by choice.
